The Michigan Department of Natural Resources (MIDNR) will conduct its annual fall lake trout survey in Lake Superior between Big Bay and Grand Island from October 19, 2026, through November 6, 2026. Operations will be conducted aboard the Research Vessel Lake Char.
Survey operations involve deploying bottom-set gill nets approximately 1,200 feet in length, extending six feet from the lakebed, and remaining set overnight in waters generally under 100 feet deep within a few miles of shore. Net locations include waters off Big Bay Point, Salmon Trout Point, Garlic Island Reef, Yellow Dog Point, Thoney Point, Granite Island, Granite Point, Partridge Island Reef, Presque Isle Harbor, Wood Island, Wood Island Shoal, and Trout Point Reef.
All nets are marked with black and orange flagged staff buoys labeled with agency identification.
The R/V Lake Char will monitor VHF-FM

The Coast Guard has transitioned to a visual Maritime Safety Information Products application for the transmission of relevant information previously contained in the published Local Notice to Mariners and Coast Guard Light List. The application, which is accessible at https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/msi, contains the most up to date maritime information overlayed on nautical charts and plotted using latitude and longitude. While the ability to print Local Notice to Mariners and Light List copies is still temporarily available, these printed products lack the positional accuracy of the electronic application and can therefore lead to relevant information being overlooked. Mariners are strongly encouraged to use the Maritime Safety Information Products application as their primary source for all information previously contained in the Local Notic

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Great Lakes National Program Office (GLNPO) will commence on or about June 01, 2026, in Torch Lake adjacent to the Lake Linden Recreation Area in the Village of Lake Linden, Houghton County, Michigan. The work area is a 3.2-acre dredge footprint covering approximately 1,300 LF along the Northwestern shoreline of Torch Lake from approximately 47°11’20.7371”N 088°24’25.0909”W to 47°11’16.2637”N 088°24’20.8101”W and a sediment processing/unloading dock located at approximately 47°10’35.0189”N 088°25’10.1927”W. Loaded and unloaded hopper barges will be towed approximately 1.2 miles between the Dredging Area and Sediment Area Processing Dock as needed.

Three turbidity monitoring buoys will be deployed in support of the work. Four (4) No Wake/No Entry buoys will be installed in the immediate vicinity of dredging work areas.
